name: No deferred revenue on annual billing
condition: Annual or multi-year billing exists, and the balance sheet has no deferred revenue account.
owner_message: You bill some customers for a year or more at once, but your balance sheet shows no deferred revenue.
fix: Book deferred revenue and recognize it ratably. Restate the affected months.

name: Revenue spikes in annual billing months
condition: Monthly revenue spikes in the same months as annual billing.
owner_message: For review: revenue rises in the same months that annual invoices go out. You may book annual contracts all at once.
fix: Recognize annual contracts over the service period.

name: Deferred revenue does not match subscriptions
condition: Deferred revenue balance differs from the subscription schedule by more than the tolerance.
owner_message: The deferred revenue on your balance sheet differs from the amount your subscription data supports by more than 5%.
fix: Build a deferred revenue roll-forward and tie it monthly.

name: Bank balance does not match balance sheet cash
condition: Bank ending balance differs from balance sheet cash at any month end by more than the tolerance.
owner_message: At one or more month ends, the bank balance and the cash on your balance sheet differ by more than $100.
fix: Reconcile the account for each month that fails.

name: Deposits do not match booked revenue
condition: Bank deposits differ from booked revenue by more than the tolerance in a month, with no explanation.
owner_message: In one or more months, bank deposits differ from your booked revenue by more than 5%.
fix: Find and book the missing or extra items, or document the timing difference.

name: Bank reconciliations missing or stale
condition: A reconciliation month is missing, or uncleared items are older than the limit.
owner_question: Does a signed bank reconciliation exist for every month, with no uncleared item older than 90 days?
owner_message: A reconciliation is missing for at least one month, or old items are still uncleared.
fix: Complete the missing reconciliations and clear old items.

name: Cash and accrual books do not tie
condition: Accrual minus cash revenue differs from the change in AR minus the change in deferred revenue by more than the tolerance.
owner_message: Your cash and accrual revenue differ by an amount that your receivables and deferred revenue do not explain.
fix: Find the entries that break the tie between the two bases.

name: Suspense or uncategorized balance
condition: A suspense, uncategorized, or ask-my-accountant account has a balance.
owner_message: An account for unsorted items still holds a balance. A buyer reads this as a sign of loose books.
fix: Reclassify each item to its correct account.

name: Negative AR, AP, or inventory balance
condition: AR, AP, or inventory has a negative balance.
owner_message: Receivables, payables, or inventory shows a negative balance. These accounts should not go below zero.
fix: Find and correct the entries that cause the negative balance.

name: Tax return revenue does not match books
condition: Tax return revenue differs from book revenue by more than the tolerance.
owner_message: The revenue on your tax return differs from the revenue in your books by more than 5%.
fix: Prepare a book-to-tax reconciliation.

name: Missing Form 1099 filings
condition: A contractor's annual payments reach the 1099 threshold for that year, and no 1099 exists.
owner_question: Did you file a Form 1099 for every contractor whose payments in a year reached the IRS threshold?
owner_message: At least one contractor reached the 1099 payment threshold in a year, and no matching 1099 filing exists.
fix: File the missing forms or document why none is due.

name: No related-party schedule
condition: A vendor or customer is related to the owner, and no related-party schedule exists.
owner_question: Do you buy from or sell to a family member or a company you own? If yes, do you keep a schedule of those deals?
owner_message: You deal with a related party and have no schedule of those deals. A buyer will ask for one.
fix: Build the schedule with terms at market rates.

name: Add-back without support
condition: An add-back has no document behind it.
owner_question: Does a document support each add-back, such as an invoice, a contract, or a ledger entry?
owner_message: At least one add-back has no document behind it. A buyer often drops such an add-back.
fix: Attach support, or the add-back moves to scope and limitations.

name: Owner pay and replacement cost
condition: Owner pay is missing from payroll, or the owner does not state replacement cost.
owner_question: What would it cost per year to hire someone to do your job, including pay and benefits?
owner_message: Your pay does not appear in payroll, or you have not stated what a replacement manager would cost.
fix: State the cost to hire a replacement. The difference becomes an adjustment.

name: Equipment purchases in operating expense
condition: A single opex entry exceeds the capitalization threshold and looks like equipment.
owner_message: For review: some large expense entries look like equipment. They may belong on the balance sheet.
fix: Review for CapEx that sits in OpEx, and the reverse.

name: Capitalized software without a policy
condition: Capitalized software sits on the balance sheet with no policy.
owner_message: Your balance sheet holds capitalized software, and no written policy or schedule supports it.
fix: Write the policy and the schedule.

name: Mixed treatment of sales commissions
condition: Commissions on annual contracts are expensed in some periods and capitalized in others.
owner_question: Do you expense commissions on annual contracts in every period, or capitalize them in every period?
owner_message: You treat commissions on annual contracts in two ways across periods. A buyer sees this as a change in policy.
fix: Pick one treatment and apply it to all periods.

name: Old receivables with no note
condition: AR over the age limit has no note.
owner_message: Some receivables are more than 90 days old, and you have given no note on them.
fix: Explain each item or write it off.

name: Customer concentration
condition: The top customer exceeds 20% of revenue, or the top 5 customers exceed 50%.
owner_message: One customer, or your five largest customers, make up a large share of revenue. A buyer will discount for this risk.
fix: No fix in the books. The guidebook explains how buyers price this risk.

name: Low gross revenue retention
condition: Annual gross revenue retention is below the minimum.
owner_message: Your customers keep less than 70% of last year's recurring revenue. A buyer will discount for this churn.
fix: No fix in the books. See the retention item in the SaaS Sellability Checklist.

name: Cash-basis books only
condition: The P&L exists on a cash basis only, and no accrual P&L exists.
owner_message: Accrual books are needed. A buyer's QoE converts cash-basis books to accrual, and the result can differ from your figures.
fix: Keep accrual books, or ask your bookkeeper for an accrual-basis P&L and balance sheet.
